segment: A0-DEF-1 was inspected against the live state and is not reproducible in the current composition; the two A0 runtime defects that were reproducible are repaired and published

a0_def_1_status.reported_defect: the recorded stop route stops the daemon before the container is removed, so the docker rm acknowledgement is unobtainable and the exact-owner cleanup stays unconfirmed
a0_def_1_status.inspection: the ORDER of the product's own operations is correct in the working path: a0_bootstrap.stop() calls runtime.stop() (which stops the container) and then retire_initial_probe() (which performs docker rm) while the daemon is still running; only afterwards does the recorded route run, and it is the route that stops the daemon. The recorded route removes the NETWORK but leaves the stopped container, which the later retirement removes.
a0_def_1_status.live_state: 13 of the 30 recorded attempts reached a written retirement (INITIAL_PROBE_RETIRED, host state retained, image retained, volumes not removed). The docker container table is EMPTY: the dedicated daemon was started for this inspection, reported no container, and was stopped again.
a0_def_1_status.the three attempts without a stop record: 121b6c56, a2039c22 and d9d17b68 stopped in phase CREATE_UNKNOWN with no stop record; their processes no longer exist and their containers are not in the table, so the stop happened but was never recorded - the record was lost when the process was killed, not because the product skipped it.
a0_def_1_status.conclusion: in the current composition the defect is not reproducible: the working path retires the initial probe with a written acknowledgement, and the table is empty. The A0 qualification itself was not re-run, so no live qualification result is claimed.
a0_def_1_status.not_changed: no code change was made for this defect, because the inspected order and the recorded evidence do not show the reported failure

a0_def_3_repaired.defect: the staged native runtime source was a mixed generation: a0_runtime.py, rootless_docker_launch.py and a0_web.py declared a daemon lifetime of 480 s, while friday-rework-docker.service and a0_profile.py declared 120 s. The runtime requires 480 s and the unit's own RuntimeMaxUSec was 2min, so every attempt was refused with host_daemon_original_deadline_changed before a container was created.
a0_def_3_repaired.relation_to_the_cleanup: the four diverging files are exactly the ones whose pinned bytes the disk cleanup of 2026-11-08 removed, so the staging area was left with a mixture of two generations
a0_def_3_repaired.repair: the staged native runtime source is published as one consistent set from the candidate, whose unit declares RuntimeMaxSec=480s and whose a0_prepare checks exactly that value
a0_def_3_repaired.verified: all five staged files are byte-identical to the candidate; proven on the isolated composition before the live application

a0_def_2_repaired.defect: the recorded stop route is a byte copy of the native runtime in a job directory and did not inherit the scoped import replacement, so 'plugins.friday_rework.supervision' did not resolve and the exact-owner cleanup stayed unconfirmed
a0_def_2_repaired.repair: both execution points of the recorded route give it the same scoped import replacement as the live module, and the composition's plugins directory is placed on sys.path
a0_def_2_repaired.verified: the recorded route of a real prior attempt was executed with the repaired replacement in the product's own environment and native_supervisor was built; before the repair the same execution failed with ModuleNotFoundError
